Add or recalculate statistics and p-values on an ALE object

Source: R/stats.R
append_stats.Rd

append_stats() calculates statistics for every stored term and outcome category without recalculating ALE. append_p() adds or replaces p-values for statistics already present. Both return an updated object; assign the result to retain it.

Usage

append_stats(
  ale_obj,
  p_values = ale_obj@params$p_values,
  ...,
  y_vals = NULL,
  aled_fun = ale_obj@params$aled_fun,
  aler_alpha = ale_obj@params$aler_alpha,
  require_p_model_match = ale_obj@params$require_p_model_match,
  silent = FALSE
)

append_p(
  ale_obj,
  p_values,
  ...,
  aler_alpha = ale_obj@params$aler_alpha,
  require_p_model_match = ale_obj@params$require_p_model_match,
  silent = FALSE
)

Arguments

ale_obj

ALE object for append_stats(), or ALE or ModelBoot object for append_p(). The existing ALE results to augment.

p_values

ALEpDist object or NULL. For append_stats(), omission inherits the distribution or NULL stored in ale_obj; explicit NULL returns statistics without p-values and removes obsolete ALER bands. For append_p(), a distribution is required and NULL is not accepted. Create distributions separately with ALEpDist(); neither function accepts "auto" or generates a distribution.

...

Not used. Subsequent arguments must be named.

y_vals

numeric vector or numeric matrix, or NULL. Complete normalization reference used by the original ALE() call: observed outcomes for numeric or ordinal outcomes, or predicted values for binary or categorical outcomes. A matrix must have one named column per outcome category; a vector is accepted for a single category. These are the original reference values even if invert_probs() was subsequently applied. Omission uses saved reference values only when they contain all original rows; otherwise supply y_vals. The 1st and 99th percentiles must lie within the saved outcome-summary limits, allowing numerical tolerance. This is a scale-consistency check; it neither verifies the entire distribution nor constrains every tail observation to the plotting limits. Supplied values are used temporarily and are not saved in the returned object.

aled_fun

character(1). Deviation method: "mad", "sd", or "var". Defaults to the method stored in ale_obj; a supplied distribution must use the same method.

aler_alpha

numeric(2) from 0 to 0.5. Increasing ALER significance thresholds, inherited from ale_obj unless overridden. Used to refresh distribution-dependent ALER bands.

require_p_model_match

logical(1). Inherited from ale_obj. If TRUE, check the supplied distribution against the stored original model identity, outcome name, and prediction type. FALSE bypasses those identity checks; deviation method, category coverage, and inversion compatibility are still required. For a ModelBoot object, inherit the outer setting when present, otherwise the full-data ALE setting; identity checks apply to the original model, and deliberately differ for its refitted bootstrap models.

silent

logical(1). If TRUE, suppress informational replacement messages. Warnings and errors remain visible.

Value

An updated object of the same class as ale_obj: ALE for append_stats(), or ALE or ModelBoot for append_p(). Neither function modifies the caller's object in place.

Details

Bootstrap statistics are calculated on each bootstrap iteration before summarization. If ale_obj was bootstrapped, append_stats() requires that it was created with output_boot_data = TRUE. Otherwise, recreate the ALE object with that option: statistics cannot be reconstructed from averaged bootstrap ALE data or pointwise confidence limits. Bootstrap significance thresholds and the mean/median choice are inherited from the object and cannot be changed here. The ALE() default of not saving bootstrap data is unchanged. For an ALE object, append_p() needs only existing statistics, so it does not require saved bootstrap data or y_vals.

For a ModelBoot object, append_stats() reports that statistics recalculation is unsupported. append_p() requires existing ALE statistics and output_boot_data = TRUE. It updates the full-data ALE object, aggregate bootstrap statistics, retained per-iteration ALE results, and distribution metadata without refitting models or recalculating ALE. Settings absent from the outer object are inherited from its full-data ALE object.

Existing statistics or p-values are replaced without an interactive prompt. An informational message reports replacement unless silent = TRUE. Estimates and bootstrap confidence intervals are preserved by append_p(); ALER bands and attached distribution metadata are refreshed. New p-value columns are appended without rearranging existing columns.

See also

ALE(), ALEpDist(), ModelBoot(), get-ALE-method

Examples

# \donttest{

  fit <- stats::lm(mpg ~ wt + am, data = mtcars)
  # ALE object created without statistics (output_stats = FALSE).
  effects <- ALE(
    fit, x_cols = c('wt', 'am'), data = mtcars,
    output_stats = FALSE, p_values = NULL
  )
  effects <- append_stats(effects)
  get(effects, stats = 'estimate')
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   term    aled aler_min    aler aler_max naled naler_min naler naler_max
#>   <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 wt    3.88   -12.1    20.9     8.80     22.9       -50  88.2      38.2
#> 2 am    0.0114  -0.0140  0.0236  0.00959   0           0   0         0  

  # Retain bootstrap data when statistics might be needed later.
  effects <- ALE(
    fit, data = mtcars, boot_it = 2, output_boot_data = TRUE,
    output_stats = FALSE, p_values = NULL, silent = TRUE
  )
  effects <- append_stats(effects, aled_fun = 'var')

  # Distribution generation is separate and can be slow.
  pd <- ALEpDist(fit, data = mtcars, aled_fun = 'var', rand_it = 100)
  effects <- append_p(effects, pd)
#> Error in validate_p_model_params(p_values, ale_obj@params$model, ale_obj@params$y_col,     ale_obj@params$pred_type): ✖ The `p_values` distribution was generated from a different model from
#>   the present one.
#> ℹ If this is deliberate (e.g., with bootstrapping), set `require_p_model_match`
#>   to "FALSE".

# }
